label: copy-phase input of digit 1 (fed-back copy of a 1 from original position >= 2)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), and only when the input is the digit token 1, i.e. the model has just fed back a copied 1. It never fires in the original phase, at <DEL>, or on any other input token. Firing is weak or absent when the copied 1 came from original position 0 or 1 (recall_idx <= 2). Its rate goes up with later recall positions and with sequences that contain more digits. The strongest activations come on the first of two consecutive 1s (e.g. ...u e b [1:1.00] [1:0.57] p), and the second 1 fires at roughly half that strength. Low-quartile activations mostly fall on 1s copied from early positions. Dev: P=0.92 R=0.91 F1=0.92 mass recall 0.97.

issues: Core claims hold. All activation is in the copy phase (share 1.000), and in_tok == '1' accounts for 100% of active steps. The original phase and <DEL> step have 0 active steps. On test, phase==2 & in_tok==1 alone gives recall 1.000.
Test scores reproduce exactly: P=0.923, R=0.908, F1=0.916, mass recall 0.966. Using recall_idx>=2 instead gives P=0.788, R=1.000, F1=0.881, matching the stated tradeoff.

The position dependence is graded, not a clean threshold. Precision among copy-phase 1s: recall_idx==2 0.32, recall_idx==3 0.83 (0.67 at L=4, 0.88 at L>=7), recall_idx==4 0.96, recall_idx>=5 0.96. The false positives (4414) and misses (5403) sit almost entirely at this boundary (recall_idx 2-3). They do not split on whether earlier originals are letters, digits or vowels (precision ~0.83 at recall_idx==3 in every split), so I found no systematic counterexample class beyond the graded position effect.

Overclaim: 'the rate goes up with sequences that contain more digits' is a confound. Per copied 1 (recall_idx>=3), precision is 0.916 with n_digits==1 and 0.930 with n_digits>=3, which is flat. The per-step rise in the profile only reflects more 1s being present.

Minor overclaim: 'low-quartile activations mostly fall on 1s copied from early positions'. In the lowest activation quartile, 72% of steps satisfy the predicate (recall_idx>=3), so most weak activations are not on 1s from positions 0-1.

The second of two consecutive 1s does still fire (precision 0.887 for prev_tok==1 & recall_idx>=3). The 'roughly half strength' claim matches the top examples (0.36-0.57 of the first 1's value), but I could only check it qualitatively.
Note: recall_idx>=3 means the input 1 is original token recall_idx-1 >= 2, so the label's 'original position >= 2' is consistent with the predicate.
